title: Prompt Drift Detection and Augmentation Pipeline
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document specifies Redwood's production pipeline for detecting prompt drift and automatically generating candidate augmentations to preserve model quality across evolving real-world inputs. It covers detection signals, augmentation heuristics, safety gating, integration with the eval harness, and an operational runbook for on-call teams.

Motivation

- Prompts observed in production evolve over time (format changes, new entity types, user intent shifts).
- Left unchecked, prompt drift causes degradations that manifest as higher latency (due to more complex completions), lower quality metrics, or increased safety/regression alerts.
- We need an automated, auditable way to surface drift, generate candidate prompt variants, and evaluate them against regression/eval suites before recommending deployment.

Scope and assumptions

- Applies to text generation and instruction-style chat endpoints backed by Redwood models (hosted + dedicated).
- Not intended for closed, customer-specific prompt templates that are governed under customer change control; those are handled via Private deployment change processes.
- Assumes token-level telemetry and request/response text retention (redacted per data-retention policy).

Architecture summary

1) Telemetry ingestion: streaming samples (1:1000 downsample by default) from production routes into the Prompt Drift Topic (Kafka).
2) Drift detector: nightly job that computes embedded-space distribution shifts and rule-based feature shifts.
3) Candidate generator: corpus-aware paraphrase and slot-filling augmentation service that proposes variants.
4) Eval harness integration: candidate variants are scored against the Production Prompt Catalog, stress bench, and targeted regression prompt sets.
5) Safety & gating: candidates must pass automated safety filters and a minimal regression delta threshold before being surfaced to SRE/ML owners.
6) Human review + rollout: triaged candidates go into a canary trial (1% traffic) with automated metrics comparison and rollback hooks.

Detection pipeline (detailed)

Input: sample stream of request prompts and metadata: route, model_id, customer_tier, timestamp. Data is normalized (strip PII, anonymize tokens).

Signals computed nightly: 
- Embedding drift (cosine): average cosine distance between embeddings of the 7-day window and baseline (30-day rolling baseline).
- Slot frequency change: sudden changes (>5x) in regex-captured slot counts (dates, numbers, product IDs).
- Prompt length distribution shift: Kullback-Leibler divergence threshold 0.08 triggers alert.
- Intent classifier shift: fraction of prompts whose predicted intent class switches compared to historical mode > 12%.
- Overt error spike: increase in bad_response_rate (defined below) by > 30% relative.

Bad_response_rate definition: percent of responses that trigger one or more of {safety_flag, eval-fallback, high-repetition, hallucination heuristic} within a 24-hour bucket.

Configuration table

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| sample_rate | 1/1000 | Fraction of incoming prompts sampled for drift detection |
| embed_model | text-embed-sim-003 | Model used for prompt embeddings |
| embed_threshold_cosine | 0.18 | Mean cosine distance over baseline to consider embedding drift |
| kl_threshold | 0.08 | KL divergence threshold for length distribution shift |
| intent_shift_pct | 12 | Percent intent-change threshold |
| slot_change_multiplier | 5 | Multiplier for slot frequency anomalies |
| bad_response_spike_pct | 30 | Percent increase to consider error spike |

Candidate generation and augmentation heuristics

- Goals: produce small set (<= 10) candidate prompt variants per drift cluster that preserve user intent while improving robustness to new inputs.
- Methods: 
  - Paraphrase via model-conditioned rephrasing (temperature 0.2) with semantic constraints to maintain intent label.
  - Slot-filling expansions: insert canonical slot examples (from FAQ/production-catalog) to handle new entity types.
  - Template normalization: unify numeric/date formats and remove brittle phrasing.
  - Contextual prompting: add short clarifying context sentences when user input becomes more ambiguous (detected via low intent-confidence).

Example candidate generation config (YAML snippet):

#!/bin/bash
cat <<'YAML' > /etc/redwood/prompt-augment.yaml
augment:
  max_candidates: 8
  paraphrase_model: text-gen-003-rewrite
  paraphrase_temp: 0.2
  preserve_intent_confidence_min: 0.85
  slot_examples_source: production-prompt-catalog
  apply_template_normalization: true
  safety_checks: ["safety-lexicon", "toxicity-check", "pii-scrub"]
YAML

Evaluation & scoring

Each candidate variant is evaluated by the eval-harness against three tiers:
1) Baseline regression set (must not worsen > 0.5% on primary metrics).
2) Targeted stress bench (must meet or exceed baseline performance for stress-specific metrics).
3) Safety/evasion suite (zero critical safety regressions).

Metrics computed per-candidate (examples):
- Accuracy / BLEU / BLEURT where ground truth exists
- Per-route latency P50/P95
- Token efficiency (tokens_out / tokens_in) and cost delta
- Safety score (0..1, 1 = safest)
- User-facing failure rate (defined by downstream validators)

Acceptance criteria (automated gate):
- Regression delta (primary_quality_metric) <= +0.5% (no degradation)
- Safety_score >= baseline - 0.01 and no critical safety flags
- Latency P95 increase <= 10% absolute
- Cost per 1k tokens increase <= 5%

Safety & human-in-the-loop review

- Any candidate failing safety checks is quarantined and assigned to Applied ML for forensics.
- Candidates that pass automated gates are batched weekly into a triage queue for ML owners and SRE review.
- Triage checklist for reviewers: intent-preservation, failure mode analysis, dataset provenance of generated examples, privacy concerns.

Canary rollout procedure (numbered steps)

1. Create augmentation bundle and register in Prompt Aug Registry: `rwctl prompts register --bundle <bundle-id>`
2. Run synthetic evaluation job: `rw-eval run --bundle <bundle-id> --suites baseline,stress,safety`
3. If job passes automated gates, schedule canary: `rw-traffic route update --route <route> --augment-bundle <bundle-id> --canary 0.01 --duration 24h`
4. Monitor SLO dashboards and the canary report for 24 hours. Key checks: quality_delta, safety_flags, latency_p95_delta, error_budget_consumption.
5. Approve rollout (gradually increase to 10%, 25%, 50%) or rollback if any prespecified alarm fires.

Predefined alarms (trigger immediate rollback):
- safety_flag_rate increase > 0.2% absolute
- primary_quality_metric degradation > 1.5%
- latency_p95 increase > 25%

Operational runbook (on-call steps)

- Pager route: prompt-drift-alerts -> applied-ml-oncall (primary) then eng-sre (secondary).
- Triage steps: 
  1. Confirm sampling and data retention windows.
  2. Review drift cluster examples from the alert.
  3. If drift is caused by a config change (client upgrade, API change), coordinate with customer success; otherwise trigger candidate generation.
  4. Kick off candidate generation job and monitor eval-harness job logs.
  5. If automated gates fail, open a regression triage ticket and follow the model-regression-forensics-playbook.

Observability and dashboards

- Dashboards: Prompt Drift Overview, Per-Route Drift Heatmap, Candidate Evaluation Summary, Canary Health.
- Alerts: embedding-drift, prompt-length-kl, intent-shift, bad-response-spike. Each alert page includes links to sampled prompts and the candidate generation job.

Integration points

- Eval harness: uses `rw-eval` job definitions and the continuous safety eval pipeline. Candidates are submitted as a `candidate_bundle` artifact.
- Quality guardrails: safety filters are shared with the runtime guardrail layer; blocked candidates are triaged into the safety review workflow.
- Quantization profiles: when augmentation changes tokenization patterns noticeably (token-length delta > 8%), notify Model Onboarding for quantization re-evaluation.
- Regression triage: failing candidates automatically create a regression ticket with reproducible harness config and sample IDs.

Metrics, SLOs and reporting cadence

- Target: detect major prompt drift (embedding distance > threshold) within 72 hours of onset.
- SLOs: false positive alert rate <= 12% (monthly), mean time from alert to candidate surfaced <= 48 hours (business days).
- Weekly report: counts of drift clusters, accepted augmentations, rejected candidates, and canary outcomes. Monthly executive summary includes cost savings and quality impact.

Ownership & escalation

- Primary owner: Applied ML (prompt-infra squad).
- Secondary owner: Eng-SRE (monitoring + alerting).
- Safety & policy reviewer: Trust & Safety.

Appendices

A. Example embedding-drift query (SQL-like pseudocode)
```
SELECT cluster_id, AVG(cosine_distance(embed, baseline_embed)) AS mean_dist
FROM prompt_embeddings
WHERE timestamp BETWEEN \"{{start}}\" AND \"{{end}}\"
GROUP BY cluster_id
HAVING mean_dist > 0.18;
```

B. Minimal reproducible eval job snippet (rw-eval JSON payload)
```
{
  "job_name": "candidate-eval-<bundle-id>",
  "suites": ["baseline", "stress", "safety"],
  "artifacts": {"candidate_bundle": "s3://redwood-eval/candidates/<bundle-id>.tgz"},
  "timeout": "2h"
}
```

C. FAQ (short)
- Q: How frequently do we run generation?
  A: Candidate generation is on-demand after a drift cluster passes thresholds; nightly background suggestions are queued weekly.
- Q: Can augmentations change customer-visible wording?
  A: Only if intent preservation is validated and no privacy concerns exist; customer-specific templates are handled separately.
- Q: What if drift is caused by upstream parser changes?
  A: Coordinate with the owning infra/service and treat the cause as a config change; do not auto-deploy augmentations without human approval.
